lead: Hypertension in pregnancy is BP ≥ 140/90 on two readings 4 h apart (one reading if ≥ 160/110). Pre-eclampsia is a placental disease of the whole body: new hypertension after 20 wk with proteinuria, or (current definition) with maternal organ damage or fetal growth restriction. Delivery is the cure.
f: Chronic: before pregnancy or before 20 wk, still high at 12 wk after birth · Gestational (PIH): after 20 wk without protein; 1 in 4 progress to PE · Pre-eclampsia: after 20 wk + proteinuria (≥ 300 mg/24 h or PCR ≥ 30 mg/mmol) · Superimposed PE: chronic HTN with new protein or organ damage · Eclampsia: PE + fits; may be the first sign, even after birth · BP: mild 140/90–149/99, moderate 150/100–159/109, severe ≥ 160/110

sc: New HTN at 34 wk, urine clear → Gestational hypertension

f: High risk (aspirin if one): previous PE, chronic HTN, kidney disease, diabetes, SLE or antiphospholipid · Moderate (aspirin if two): first pregnancy, age 40 or more, BMI over 30, family history, twins, interval over 10 years · Aspirin 75 mg at night, 12–36 wk · Calcium 1.5–2 g/day from 20 wk if dietary intake is low

Often no symptoms: ask about headache, flashes, epigastric pain, vomiting · Sudden face and hand oedema, hyperreflexia, clonus, RUQ tenderness, small fundus · Severe PE (any one): BP ≥ 160/110 · severe headache, visual disturbance, clonus · epigastric or RUQ pain, raised AST/ALT · platelets below 100, haemolysis · oliguria, raised creatinine · pulmonary oedema · severe FGR

sc: RUQ pain, shock, falling Hb → Liver capsule rupture

f: Urine dipstick → PCR or 24 h protein · FBC (platelets), creatinine, uric acid (rises with severity), LFT, LDH, film; clotting if platelets low · Fetus: growth scan, liquor, umbilical artery Doppler, CTG · Absent or reversed end-diastolic flow = deliver soon

sc: PE at 32 wk, reversed EDF → Steroids, MgSO₄, deliver (usually CS)

f: Differential: eclampsia, epilepsy, hypoglycaemia, meningitis, cerebral venous thrombosis, cerebral malaria · Test glucose and malaria in every fit; unsure: MgSO₄ + IV artesunate · Maternal: eclampsia, intracranial haemorrhage (leading cause of death), HELLP, DIC, AKI, pulmonary oedema, abruption, PPH · Fetal: FGR, oligohydramnios, prematurity (mostly iatrogenic), stillbirth

Mild: clinic, BP every 2 wk · Moderate: clinic or admit, BP 2–3 times a week, bloods weekly · Severe: admit, HDU, BP every 15 min · Labetalol first (200 mg 8-hourly; IV when severe; not in asthma) · Nifedipine 20 mg twice daily (max 60 mg/day) · Methyldopa 250 mg 8-hourly (change after birth: depression) · Severe: hydralazine 5 mg IV over 10–15 min every 15 min, with 500 mL saline first · Never ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics · Target 135/85 (NICE)

sc: BP 170/115 at 33 wk with headache → IV hydralazine (or labetalol) + MgSO₄
On enalapril, now 8 wk pregnant → Switch to labetalol

f: Prevents and treats eclamptic fits · Loading 4 g IV over 5–15 min, then 1 g/h for 24 h after birth or the last fit · Toxicity in order: loss of knee jerk → respiratory depression (RR below 12) → cardiac arrest · Keep urine ≥ 30 mL/h (kidneys clear it) · Antidote: 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV slowly · Fit on MgSO₄: extra 2 g IV · Fluids ≤ 80 mL/h: leaky capillaries cause pulmonary oedema

sc: On MgSO₄, reflexes absent, RR 16 → Stop the infusion, check the level
tr: MgSO₄ prevents fits; it does not lower BP

f: Eclampsia: call for help, left lateral, airway, O₂; do not hold her down · MgSO₄ 4 g IV then 1 g/h (diazepam only if no magnesium) · Lower BP if ≥ 160/110; check glucose and malaria; catheter · Deliver once stable (within 6–12 h) · HELLP: haemolysis (LDH raised), elevated liver enzymes, platelets below 100; BP may be only mildly raised; treat as severe PE and deliver; risks DIC, liver rupture

tr: Epigastric pain and vomiting at 34 wk = HELLP until proven otherwise, not gastritis
HELLP is severe whatever the BP

f: Gestational HTN or PE without severe features: 37 wk (NICE); local units often 38 wk · Severe PE, eclampsia, HELLP: deliver once stable, at any gestation; steroids under 34 wk · Induction preferred; CS if the cervix is unfavourable and birth is not near, or fetal distress · Continuous CTG; epidural if platelets over 80 · Third stage: oxytocin, no ergometrine · After birth: fits still possible (MgSO₄ 24 h); BP peaks on days 3–5; wean drugs; 6-wk review

sc: Fit on day 2 after birth, BP 160/110 → Postpartum eclampsia
PPH in a woman with PE → Oxytocin, not ergometrine
